findings.novelty: Existing floating-dependency risk independently confirmed; this round adds exact release-branch evidence and the missing executable integration step. Not a newly discovered wx implementation bug.
findings.title: The reviewed wx behavior is not selected by Bambu, and wx2 on master would reach uncorrected release branches
findings.trigger: A clean Bambu dependency build uses the current recipe. Today that selects bambulab/wxWidgets master rather than either fork fix. If wx2 subsequently merges to that master, an uncorrected release/20260929 (exact local head f5e51a20bd328d4a043af9344825d7347270c2c9) dependency rebuild at GTK font DPI 144 obtains the nonidentity conversion too.
findings.outcome: Today the reviewed GTK fixes are absent from the default fetched dependency; later the older release code scales already measured pixel widths again. Updating Bambu master with #5 does not fix that release. Existing warnings document the gate but do not provide a reproducible dependency selection or protect release recipes.
findings.proof: Exact source extracts and commands.json. Both local release heads b506005bc4ee62124e24bf00e0f58656db3646a6 and f5e51a20bd328d4a043af9344825d7347270c2c9 have GIT_TAG master. The newer release retains FromDIP(GetSize().GetWidth() - 120 - measured child widths), whereas app #5 removes the conversion around measured widths. With W=1000, child widths=100/20 and font scale=1.5, release max-status width is min(1140,900)=900 instead of corrected min(700,900)=700. This arithmetic illustration is not a native rendering run.
findings.smallest_practical_fix: Add a separate small Bambu dependency-pin/integration draft: pin an exact reachable wx SHA containing both reviewed GTK changes AND current upstream abb5426. A fork-only draft must use the fork URL when its SHA is not reachable from bambulab/wxWidgets. Keep #5 independent. Before wx2 goes to upstream master, pin each supported uncorrected release branch to each branch's last validated pre-wx2 revision (the frozen e2fa9bd or, after validating its Windows change, abb5426), or backport #5. If maintainers cannot protect release builds, carry wx2 on an opt-in wx branch and pin only the corrected app to it; do not merge wx2 to shared master. Legacy immutable tags need a documented build-time source pin or archived dependency; do not retag them.
findings.verification_needed: Review the concrete pin diff and source SHA ancestry/blob contents; confirm the SHA is fetchable from its declared repository; inspect supported release recipes at exact heads; clean rebuild dependency and application together on GTK3; compare 96/144 font DPI and GDK scale 1/2. The updated wx contains a Windows WebView change, so obtain a Windows build/text-scale smoke check before claiming that integration validated there. Keep native macOS/Windows results distinct from source checks.
findings.blocking_scope: Blocks wx2-to-shared-master and claiming a reproducible completed integration. Does not block independent wx1 or merging app #5 before the dependency change.

findings.novelty: New wording issue independently checked in exact source.
findings.title: wx1 body overstates its wrapped-label exclusion

locations.quote: Wrapped labels and other widgets retain their existing path.

findings.trigger: A reviewer reads the body as promising that wrapped wxStaticText never reaches the new invalidation branch.
findings.outcome: wxStaticText::DoGetBestSize temporarily disables GTK line wrapping before delegating measurement and reenables it afterward, so wrapped static texts can reach the new branch. This is not evidence of a layout defect; the scope statement is too broad.
findings.smallest_practical_fix: Replace the scope sentence with: “The check runs only when GTK measures a label without wrapping; other widget types keep their existing path.” Keep the GTK4 exclusion statement. Mention wrapped wxStaticText in detailed evidence only if useful.
findings.verification_needed: Read the replacement body alongside stattext.cpp:237–251 and control.cpp:356–377. Native wrapped-label tests remain useful but are not required to verify this wording fix.

limitations: No network, delegation, build, native probe, GUI interaction or repository writes.
Python arithmetic transcription and lexical thread scan are limited checks, not compiled/native proofs.
No Windows/macOS, GTK2/GTK4, shared-library or native Wayland runtime approval.
Local release refs are sampled recipes, not an exhaustive inventory of supported branches, forks or tags.
No claim of future upstream commits beyond abb542694ef4534a50e65c5b877b2774d02952ae; network prohibited.
